title: Indian Film Festival of Melbourne Opens With Star-Studded Lineup and Special Honours
excerpt: The 17th IFFM kicks off today with nominations spanning nine languages, and awards for Dulquer Salmaan, Rishab Shetty, Pankaj Tripathi, and Rani Mukerji.
body:
• The 17th Indian Film Festival of Melbourne (IFFM) runs August 13-23, 2026, with nominations spanning nine languages and eight Best Film contenders including Kantara: A Legend Chapter 1
  • Dulquer Salmaan attends as Guest of Honour while Rishab Shetty receives the Leadership in Cinema Award for the Kantara franchise
  • Pankaj Tripathi earns the Artist of Distinction honour and Rani Mukerji receives an Honorary Doctor of Letters from La Trobe University
  • The nominations feature 15 women filmmakers, 17 women-led stories, and six queer narratives across competitive categories

The 17th Indian Film Festival of Melbourne opens today in Australia's cultural capital, bringing together some of Indian cinema's most celebrated names for 11 days of screenings, premieres, masterclasses, and awards.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=H1CIsVTGc8U

Running August 13-23 with support from the Victorian Government, IFFM has cemented its position as the largest annual celebration of Indian cinema outside India. This year's edition features a stacked nomination slate spanning nine languages, special honours for four marquee guests, and a lineup that underscores the industry's growing reach across borders.

Star-Studded Acting Categories

The Best Performance (Male) category reads like a who's who of Indian cinema: Aamir Khan, Dulquer Salmaan, Mammootty, Ranveer Singh, Rishab Shetty, Sanjay Mishra, Ahaan Pandey, and Bhuman Bhargav Das. On the female side, nominees include Rani Mukerji, Yami Gautam Dhar, Neena Gupta, Kirti Kulhari, Kalyani Priyadarshan, Rajshri Deshpande, Rituparna Sengupta, and Aneet Padda.

The Best Film category features eight contenders — Haq, Jarann, Kantara: A Legend Chapter 1, Lokah Chapter 1: Chandra, Saiyaara, Sitaare Zameen Par, Sharthopor, and The Great Shamsuddin Family — representing multiple regional industries and genres.

Rishab Shetty stands out with recognition across three categories: Best Film, Best Director, and Best Performance (Male) for the Kantara sequel, making him one of the most-nominated artists at this year's festival.

Four Special Honours

Beyond the competitive categories, IFFM 2026 is recognizing four artists with individual awards that highlight the range of Indian cinema's impact.

Dulquer Salmaan attends as one of the festival's Guests of Honour, celebrated for a career spanning Malayalam, Tamil, Telugu, and Hindi cinema. Festival Director Mitu Bhowmick Lange AM described him as an artist "who has effortlessly crossed languages, industries and genres while remaining deeply committed to meaningful storytelling."

"Storytelling has always been my way of celebrating our culture, our traditions and the communities that inspire us. It is incredibly meaningful to see stories rooted in our heritage resonate with audiences across the world."

— Rishab Shetty, Leadership in Cinema Award recipient

Rishab Shetty receives the Leadership in Cinema Award for expanding the global conversation around Indian cinema through the Kantara franchise, which draws on the folklore, indigenous beliefs, and spiritual traditions of coastal Karnataka.

Pankaj Tripathi earns the Artist of Distinction honour for his body of work across film and streaming. "Coming from a small village in Bihar, I never imagined that the stories I would become a part of would one day travel across the world and be celebrated in this manner," Tripathi said.

Rani Mukerji will receive an Honorary Doctor of Letters from La Trobe University during the festival. La Trobe Chancellor John Brumby called her "an exceptional recipient" whose work "has transcended entertainment to spark important conversations around social justice, equality and inclusion."

Diversity Across the Nominations

The festival's commitment to representation is reflected in the numbers: 15 women filmmakers feature across categories, 17 women-led stories are nominated, and six queer narratives are included in the competitive slate. Best Director nominees include Ashwiny Iyer Tiwari (System), Rima Das (Not a Hero), and Shazia Iqbal (Dhadak 2) alongside Rishab Shetty, RS Prasanna (Sitaare Zameen Par), Mohit Suri (Saiyaara), Chandrasish Ray (Porshi), and Ramalingam Gowtham (Members of the Problematic Family).

Streaming content also features prominently, with series nominations for Kohrra: Season 2, Matka King, Sapne Vs Everyone, Freedom at Midnight: Season 2, and The Ba***ds of Bollywood.

Premieres and Industry Moves

Ramalingam Gowtham's Members of the Problematic Family opens the festival, while Vikram Phadnis' Pal Bhar Ke Liye heads to Melbourne for its world premiere. In a major industry announcement tied to IFFM, Aamir Khan Productions and Kabir Khan Films confirmed Silkyara 41, a film based on the Uttarakhand tunnel rescue, in partnership with Australia's Mind Blowing Films.

A Stage for Diaspora Audiences

For the Indian diaspora in Australia and across the Asia-Pacific, IFFM has evolved from a cultural event into a legitimate industry gathering where films gain international visibility, deals are struck, and artists engage directly with overseas audiences. This year's combination of mainstream star power, regional-language diversity, and industry milestones reflects a festival that has matured into one of Indian cinema's most important annual stops outside the subcontinent.
nri_angle: IFFM is the largest celebration of Indian cinema outside India, serving as a cultural touchstone for the Indian diaspora in Australia and globally, with events, premieres, and industry connections that bring Indian stories to international audiences.
